title: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

questions.question: Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:1 (ESV): "Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the Lord!"

questions.question: How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to your what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:9 (ESV): "By guarding it according to your word."

questions.question: I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:11 (ESV): "that I might not sin against you."

questions.question: Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:18 (ESV): "Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law."

questions.question: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:105 (ESV): "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path."

questions.question: Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation how often?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:97 (ESV): "It is my meditation all the day."

questions.question: The unfolding of your words gives light; it imparts understanding to the what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:130 (ESV): "it imparts understanding to the simple."

questions.question: Great peace have those who love your law; nothing can make them do what?
Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth how long?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:160 (ESV): "The sum of your word is truth, and every one of your righteous rules endures forever."

questions.question: Let my soul live and praise you, and let your rules help whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:175 (ESV): "...and let your rules help me."

questions.question: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible. How many verses does it have?
The Psalm is divided into sections, each corresponding to a letter of which alphabet?
questions.explanation: It is an acrostic poem based on the Hebrew alphabet.

questions.question: Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep your what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:67 (ESV): "Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep your word."

questions.question: It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn your what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:71 (ESV): "...that I might learn your statutes."

questions.question: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for I do not forget your what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 119:176 (ESV): "...for I do not forget your commandments."

key_verse_text: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
